title: Compulsory English: Unit-wise Objective Question Bank

toc.title: 8.1 Where objective items sit in the paper

html:
The Grade 10 English paper carries 75 marks in three hours, and a large share of those marks are objective: true/false, multiple-choice, matching, gap-filling and one-word items. They appear in the reading questions on the two textbook passages, in the vocabulary question on the long unseen passage, and in the ten grammar items. This chapter gives practice items for all 18 units of the Grade 10 book, with an answer key and a short reason for every item.

About the labels in this chapter

Every item here is an original practice item written to the pattern of the SEE English paper and to the facts of the book chapters in this series. None is claimed to be a question from a particular year's paper. A book that prints a board year beside each item is usually guessing, and a wrong label teaches you to trust the wrong thing.

8.1 Where objective items sit in the paper

The Curriculum Development Centre (CDC) specification grid for Grade 10 English (2080 curriculum) divides the 75 marks as follows. Check the current grid on the CDC site before the examination, because boards can adjust small details such as the marks of a single task.

Part Marks What is tested Objective item types
Reading 1: seen text, about 100 words 5 comprehension of a textbook passage one type, often true/false or gap-fill
Reading 2: seen text, about 200 words 10 comprehension two types, such as multiple-choice and short answer
Reading 3: unseen text, about 200 words 10 story, notice, advertisement, letter, news story two types
Reading 4: unseen text, about 300 words 15 essay, article, biography, review three types, including vocabulary
Writing: guided and free tasks 25 five-to-nine-mark writing tasks none (marked on a scale)
Grammar 10 ten one-mark items reproduction and multiple-choice in context

How to use the bank

Cover the key and answer the items of one unit in five minutes. Mark them. For every error, go back to the passage in the book chapter and find the sentence that gives the answer. For objective reading items, the answer is always in the text; your own opinion earns nothing.

8.2 Reading items by unit

Each unit below tests the two textbook passages. Items marked T/F are true/false.

5. True.

8.3 Vocabulary items

The long unseen passage (Reading 4) always carries a vocabulary item; the seen passages test words from the book. Choose the best meaning or fill the gap.

A. Choose the word closest in meaning to the underlined word (1 mark each)

  1. The mountain village has a calm serene atmosphere.anoisybpeacefulccrowdedddirty
  2. She was obsessed with her phone.abored bybunable to stop thinking aboutcafraid ofdangry with

  4. The altitude of Kathmandu is about 1,400 m.awidthbheight above sea levelctemperaturedpopulation
  5. The shopkeeper swerved to avoid the cow.astoppedbturned suddenly asidecshouteddjumped
  6. The rice was scarce after the flood.aplentifulbhard to findccheapdtasty

B. Choose the opposite (1 mark each)

  1. ancientaoldbmoderncruineddvaluable
  2. expandagrowbshrinkcshoutdcover
  3. generousakindbselfishcrichdbright
  4. brightadullbshinyccleverdwarm

C. Fill the gap with the best word from the box (1 mark each)

Box: determination, valuable, humble, peaceful, perseverance

  2. In spite of fame, the chef remained ____ and thanked his teachers.
  3. Walt Disney's ____ is a good lesson for every student.
  4. The ____ countryside is a pleasant escape from the noisy city.

D. Prefixes, suffixes and compounds (1 mark each)

  1. Add a prefix to make the opposite of possible. 16. Add a suffix to care to mean "without care". 17. Make an adjective from danger. 18. Write the compound word from Unit 9 that means "the act of giving presents". 19. The word cardboard is made of two nouns. Write them.

12. humble.

13. perseverance (or determination).

19. card + board.

Compound words

The SEE checks compound items against the words in the book: gift-giving, heart-warming, cardboard, flower etiquette, break-up, fortune-telling, newly-wed. Learn them as a list.

8.4 Grammar items by unit

The CDC grid asks ten one-mark grammar items covering articles, prepositions, tenses, connectives, question tags, reported speech, voice, conditionals, subject-verb agreement, relative clauses and causatives. Practise by unit; the sets below follow the book's order.

Reported speech: statements, questions, commands (Units 1 to 3)

Change into reported speech (1 mark each).

  1. "I am tired," said Ram. 2. "We will go to Pokhara tomorrow," said the girls. 3. "Did you finish the work?" the teacher asked Sita. 4. "Where do you live?" he asked me. 5. "Please close the door," she said to him. 6. "Don't touch the wire," the mother told the child. 7. "The earth moves round the sun," the teacher said. 8. "I have lost my pen," said Hari.
Answers: reported speech

1. Ram said that he was tired.

2. The girls said that they would go to Pokhara the next day.

3. The teacher asked Sita if (whether) she had finished the work.

4. He asked me where I lived.

5. She requested him to close the door.

6. The mother told the child not to touch the wire.

7. The teacher said that the earth moves round the sun. (no backshift for a universal truth)

8. Hari said that he had lost his pen.

Modals and imperatives (Unit 4)

Choose the correct word (1 mark each).

  1. You ____ wear a helmet; it is the law.acanbmustcmaydmight
  2. "____ I borrow your pen?"aMaybMustcWoulddShall to
  3. He ____ have missed the bus; he is not here.amustbcancshoulddwill
  4. You look pale. You ____ see a doctor.ashouldbcan'tcuseddshall
  5. ____ you help me with this bag?aCouldbMight tocOughtdDare
  6. She ____ to get up early when she was a child.ahasbhadcmustdwould be
Answers: modals

1. (b) must — legal compulsion.

2. (a) May — permission.

3. (a) must — certainty.

4. (a) should — advice.

5. (a) Could — polite request.

6. (b) had — had to is the past of have to.

Conditionals (Unit 5)

Fill in with the correct form (1 mark each).

  1. If you heat ice, it _ (melt). 2. If it rains tomorrow, we (stay) at home. 3. If I _ (be) a bird, I would fly to Lukla. 4. If she had studied, she (pass). 5. _ you hurry, you will miss the bus. (unless/if) 6. I will lend you the book provided you (return) it. 7. If he _ (leave) earlier, he would have caught the bus. 8. I known, I would have come. (inverted)
Answers: conditionals

1. melts (zero conditional).

2. will stay.

3. were (second conditional uses were for all persons).

4. would have passed.

5. Unless — Unless you hurry means If you do not hurry, and the result is that you miss the bus.

6. return (present after provided).

7. had left.

8. Had.

Present continuous and reasons (Unit 6)

Choose the correct word (1 mark each).

  1. Look! The chef ____ the soup.astirsbis stirringcstirreddhas stirring
  2. We ____ to Pokhara next week; the tickets are booked.agobare goingcwentdhave gone
  3. He stayed at home ____ he was ill.abecausebbecause ofcin spite ofdso
  4. He stayed at home ____ his illness.abecausebbecause ofcalthoughdbut
  5. She went to the market ____ buy vegetables.aforbin order tocsodbecause
  6. They are saving money ____ they can buy a house.aso thatbin ordercalthoughdto
Answers: reasons

1. (b) — action happening now.

2. (b) — planned future.

3. (a) — because + clause.

4. (b) — because of + noun.

5. (b) — purpose with the base verb.

6. (a) — so that + clause.

Articles and advice (Unit 7)

Fill in with a, an, the or X for no article (1 mark each).

  1. He is _ honest boy. 2. She works at university in Kathmandu. 3. _ Sun rises in the east. 4. Ram plays football every evening. 5. I saw _ one-eyed man. 6. Himalayas are in the north of Nepal. 7. You _ keep your password secret. (should/must not) 8. You share your password with strangers. (must not/should)
Answers: articles

1. an (honest begins with a vowel sound).

2. a (university begins with a consonant sound, /j/).

3. The (unique).

4. X (games take no article).

5. a (one begins with /w/).

6. The (mountain range).

7. should (advice).

8. must not (prohibition).

Passive voice (Units 8 and 10)

Change into the passive voice (1 mark each).

  1. Sita writes a letter. 2. The farmers are planting rice. 3. They built a bridge last year. 4. The teacher has corrected the exercise books. 5. Who wrote this poem? 6. Someone will finish the work tomorrow. 7. The committee should have decided the matter. 8. They are showing a film tonight.
Answers: passive

1. A letter is written by Sita.

2. Rice is being planted by the farmers.

3. A bridge was built last year.

4. The exercise books have been corrected by the teacher.

5. By whom was this poem written? (or: Who was this poem written by?)

6. The work will be finished by someone tomorrow. (or: The work will be finished tomorrow.)

7. The matter should have been decided by the committee.

8. A film is being shown tonight.

Present perfect and agreement (Units 10 and 11)

Choose the correct word (1 mark each).

  1. I ____ here since 2020.alivebhave livedcam livingdlived
  2. She has been waiting ____ two hours.asincebforcfromdby
  3. A number of students ____ absent today.aisbarecwasdhas been
  4. The number of students ____ increasing.aarebiscweredhave
  5. Neither the teacher nor the students ____ present.awasbwerecisdhas
  6. Each of the boys ____ a ticket.ahavebhascaredwere
  7. He doesn't know, _? (tag) 8. Nobody came, _ they?
Answers: perfect and agreement

1. (b) — since + point in time takes the present perfect.

2. (b) — for + period.

3. (b) — a number of is plural.

4. (b) — the number of is singular.

5. (b) — verb agrees with the nearer subject (students).

6. (b) — each is singular.

7. does he.

8. did — nobody makes the clause negative, so the tag is positive; the pronoun is they.

Future forms and connectives (Units 12 and 13)

Choose the correct word (1 mark each).

  1. The train ____ at 6 a.m. tomorrow (timetable).aleavesbis leavingcwill have leftdleft
  2. Look at those clouds. It ____ rain.awillbis going tocshalldis raining
  3. By next year I ____ my SEE.awill passbwill have passedcpassdam passing
  4. ____ it was raining, we played football.aBecausebAlthoughcSodUnless
  5. ____ the heavy rain, the match went on.aAlthoughbDespitecThoughdEven though
  6. The road is useful. ____, it harms the environment.aHoweverbBecausecAlthoughdDespite
Answers: future and connectives

1. (a) timetable.

2. (b) — plan or prediction from evidence.

3. (b) — completed before a future time.

4. (b).

5. (b) — despite is followed by a noun phrase.

6. (a) — however takes a comma and starts a new sentence. Never use although … but together.

Question tags and relative clauses (Units 14 and 15)

Add a question tag or fill in the relative word (1 mark each).

  1. You are a student, _? 2. Let's go home, ? 3. Open the window, _? 4. I am late, ? 5. The girl _ won the prize is my cousin. 6. This is the pen I bought yesterday. 7. The man _ car was stolen called the police. 8. Pokhara, is a lake city, attracts tourists. 9. He never lies, ____?
Answers: tags and relatives

1. aren't you.

2. shall we.

3. will you.

4. aren't I.

5. who.

6. which (or that).

7. whose.

8. which (non-defining; that is not allowed).

9. does he — never is negative in sense, so the tag is positive.

Prepositions (Units 15 and 16)

Fill in with the correct preposition (1 mark each).

  1. The class starts _ 10 a.m. 2. He was born Monday. 3. They came to Nepal _ 2015. 4. She is afraid dogs. 5. I am good _ mathematics. 6. He divided the money his two sons. 7. We stayed _ Friday Sunday. (from … to) 8. The book is ____ the table.
Answers: prepositions

1. at (clock time).

2. on (day).

3. in (year).

4. of (afraid of).

5. at (good at).

6. between (two persons).

7. from … to.

8. on (surface).

Choose the correct word (1 mark each).

  1. She sings ____.abeautifulbbeautifullycbeautydmore beauty
  2. He is the ____ boy in the class.atallerbtallestcmore talldmost tall
  3. This book is ____ than that one.agoodbbettercbestdmore good
  4. She ____ the barber cut her hair.ahadbmade tocwasdgot to
  5. He ____ his car repaired yesterday.ahadbmadecletdtold
  6. The teacher ____ us write an essay.amadebgotcwas madedforced to
Answers: adverbs and causatives

1. (b) — adverb of manner.

2. (b) — superlative of a short adjective.

3. (b) — irregular good, better, best.

4. (a) — have + person + base verb.

5. (a) — have + thing + past participle.

6. (a) — make + person + base verb.

Chapter summary

  • The paper is 75 marks in 3 hours: Reading 40 (5 + 10 + 10 + 15), Writing 25 and Grammar 10. Objective and short-answer items fill most of the reading part.
  • Answer reading items from the text. Read the question first, then find the line.
  • Tag questions reverse polarity: aren't I, shall we (after let's), will you (after commands), they (after nobody, everyone).
  • Reported speech steps the tense back after a past reporting verb but not for universal truths; commands take to or not to.
  • Conditionals: zero (present, present), first (present, will), second (past, would), third (past perfect, would have). Unless means if not.
  • A number of is plural; the number of is singular; each, everyone are singular; with neither … nor the verb agrees with the nearer subject.
  • Passive is be + past participle in the tense of the active verb; use by + agent only when it matters.
